technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: historical classifications are sparse, heavily use generic categories such as 'other', and may encode post-routing corrections, sensitive allegations or inconsistent local taxonomies

training_data.observation_unit: one citizen manifestation, service request or administrative expedient at initial intake
training_data.input_data: text available at submission time, channel metadata, citizen-selected fields when present, controlled taxonomy and only non-sensitive routing context permitted for the task
training_data.target_or_reward: human-confirmed manifestation type, subject, responsible body or bounded extracted fields
training_data.label_source: final classifications and corrections made by authorized intake or treatment staff; consistency and reuse rights must be audited
training_data.prediction_time: after submission and before routing, triage or substantive treatment
training_data.expected_volume: unknown and organization-specific; class and taxonomy coverage must be measured before training
training_data.class_balance: unknown; generic categories and high-frequency services are likely dominant, while sensitive or unusual manifestations may be rare
training_data.historical_coverage: partially plausible because Fala.BR and protocol systems retain classifications, but label quality, versioned taxonomies and local portability are unknown
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based and organization-disjoint holdouts, with separate evaluation for rare classes, taxonomy revisions and ambiguous multi-label cases
training_data.leakage_risks: using final responsible unit, treatment notes, investigation outcome, response text, reclassification or closure fields unavailable at intake
training_data.representativeness_risks: regional language, literacy, accessibility, channel, service taxonomy, agency responsibilities and changes in public-service catalogs
training_data.feedback_loop: model suggestions can anchor human classification and gradually reproduce its own prior errors or suppress rare categories
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: manifestations may contain personal, sensitive or whistleblower data; minimization, access control, retention, purpose limitation and human review are mandatory
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: structured intake, controlled vocabulary search, mandatory fields, deterministic routing rules, synonym dictionaries and manual classification

portfolio_comparison.reason: The remaining mechanism is generic bounded text classification and routing. It does not create a distinct actor-process-outcome pattern beyond current public platforms, configurable workflow products and repository classification or extraction patterns.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt and configure Fala.BR or equivalent public-service workflow platforms, using structured taxonomies and human confirmation. A compact local classifier may be an implementation option for uncovered municipal integrations, not a separate solution opportunity.

research.findings: The Fala.BR rollout published on 2 April 2026 already automates manifestation-type classification and announced suggestions for subject, destination body and public service. Current official material also documents a very large controlled taxonomy with frequent generic or missing classifications, confirming the label-quality risk. Municipal conversational protocol systems and commercial ombudsman platforms cover the same intake and routing outcome.
